text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Deputy army chief: army takes into account chance of military confrontation with Syria in 1997.
- Jews purchased another home in Christian quarter of Jerusalem's Old City.
- Arafat: Hebron deal to be signed in the coming days; Ross returns on Monday.
- Israel's coordinator in the West Bank and Gaza Oren Shachor quits.
JERUSALEM POST
- Strike strands thousands at Ben-Gurion airport.
- Arafat: Hebron deal by Tuesday.
- Deputy army chief: Israeli army prepared for any surprise Syrian attack.
- Former Bank of Israeli governor, Michael Bruno, dies at 64.
- Analysts: Wall Street more sceptical of Israeli IPOs.
MAARIV
- Defence Minister Mordechai: "I'm not willing to ignite the whole Middle East over a shack in Hebron".
- Netanyahu: "We will privatise the Broadcasting Authority."
- Strike today at Israeli ports, phone services disrupted.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Army officials see rise in chance of war with Syria in 1997.
GLOBES
- Treasury: 1997 defence budget grew in real terms.
